pages.text: "A boat!" Kkiruk called. Dari slid to the dock as a white boat puttered closer. "Dad, I want a ride around the island!"

A lighthouse inspector stepped off—a black cormorant with a notebook beneath her wing. "You may ride, but wear this." She offered a little life jacket. Dari wriggled. "It's a bother! Can't I ride without it?"
Dad put it on Dari and clicked the fastener shut. "No jacket, no sailing." Pouting, Dari boarded. The boat puttered away.
A wave splashed and tilted the boat. Dari rolled sideways into the water! Dad gripped the jacket's back loop and pulled him aboard. "The jacket held me!" It had kept his body afloat.

Dad took off the wet jacket and squeezed out water. The inspector sat beside Dari. "Not a bother—a hug in the water! Everyone aboard wears one. Shall I put your name in my notebook, too?" Dari lifted his head.
She taught three steps. "One, flippers through! Two, click it shut! Three, say 'Ready to go!'" Dari gripped the jacket. "I can do it!" She smiled. "Click your life jacket!"
Dari put both flippers through and clicked it shut himself. "Dad, all on! Ready to go!" He slapped his tail. Click your life jacket!
The boat circled the island. Even another wave didn't frighten Dari. "Not scary with my jacket on!" The inspector wrote, "Dari—life jacket passed!"
Now he followed the steps for every boat ride. "One, flippers through! Two, click it shut! Three, ready to go!" Next time on Dad's boat, Dari put his jacket on first.
At the dock, Dad hugged him. "You kept the jacket promise yourself!" A life jacket wasn't a bother. It was a hug in the water. "Click your life jacket!" Dari smiled in Dad's arms.
